purpose: Vehicle-specific TPMS relearn method classification for TireCare Logic / ValveLogic.

rules.rule: Never assign a relearn method by brand alone. Year, model, platform, TPMS architecture, and sensor type can change the procedure.
Determine whether the vehicle uses direct TPMS wheel sensors or indirect TPMS wheel-speed calibration before recommending a sensor or relearn procedure.
A programmable aftermarket sensor may require cloning or programming before vehicle relearn. Relearn and sensor programming are separate operations.

verifiedExamples.confirmation: Horn chirp at each learned position; double horn after final position.
verifiedExamples.notes: Vehicle is placed into TIRE LEARNING ACTIVE mode and a TPMS relearn tool is used near each valve stem.

verifiedExamples.driveTime: Approximately 15 minutes after reset on documented applications
verifiedExamples.notes: Some current Ford applications use an in-vehicle reset followed by automatic sensor relearn during driving. Other Ford applications use explicit sensor training, so do not generalize this procedure to all Ford vehicles.
Documented Ford applications can enter training mode and learn positions by pressure change. Procedure varies by model/year.

verifiedExamples.driveTime: Approximately 30 minutes cumulative driving at 30-65 mph after calibration is initiated
verifiedExamples.notes: This application calibrates the TPMS rather than learning individual wheel pressure sensors.

verifiedExamples.driveTime: May require up to 20 minutes above 15 mph for updated pressure information to be received
verifiedExamples.notes: Documented example of drive-based TPMS updating. Exact sensor replacement/relearn procedure still must be verified by model/year.
